fe201a4b996ee2bef8022754d9032103cf94d825: A resort on a human scale, Gavarnie-Gèdre prides itself on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 32 km of runs are perfectly suited to a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or for skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Gavarnie-Gèdre's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a laid-back atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for getting children started on skiing. Gavarnie-Gèdre's altitude (1,350 m at the base, 2,400 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The 34€ day lift pass remains reasonable for the quality of the ski area on offer. Counting accommodation, skiing and meals, Gavarnie-Gèdre suits those who want a lovely week without the final bill making them keel over. In short: Gavarnie-Gèdre is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suitable for everyone. It's hard to have a bad stay here.

fe4787cd9e2b65c4bd9983e9f40b14e76f4db56a: A resort on a human scale, Gemsstock (Andermatt) focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Technical terrain is king at Gemsstock (Andermatt): with 55 black runs and 45 red runs on offer, confident skiers will find plenty to test themselves. Off-piste and freeride skiing are often enjoyed in excellent conditions thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. With a summit at 2961 m and a village at 1444 m, snow reliability at Gemsstock (Andermatt) is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause shortages early in the season, but conditions soon recover with the first serious snowfalls. The budget for a stay at Gemsstock (Andermatt) is clearly high: €94 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
